questions.question:
**In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains a grammatical error.**

People has been warning in advance about the coming economic crisis.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'has been warning'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• According to **the subject-verb agreement rule**, if the subject is singular, the verb must be singular and if the subject is plural, the verb must also be plural. 
 
• **Examples, **
 
 
• These **clothes are** too small for me.
 
• **People travel **overseas these days.
 
• Some **people were** hurt.
 
 
 
• The word '**people**' is a** plural noun.** So, it should be followed by a **plural verb. (have)**
 
• Thus, 'have been warned' is the correct usage.
 
• We need to use a verb warned because the doer of the verb warned is somebody else hence we need to use a past participle of the verb. As the warning has been given to the people by somebody else. Hence, the correct phrase is have been warned.
 
• Therefore, **option 4** is the correct answer.

**Correct Sentence:** *People **have been warned** in advance about the coming economic crisis.*

questions.question:
**In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.**

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the above-given sentence,** 'wondered'** will be used.
 
• It is so because **'When two actions occur in the past, one after the other, the first action is expressed in Past perfect tense and the second action is expressed in Simple past tense'.**
 
• **For Examples:-**
 
 
• The patient **had died** before the doctor **came**.
 
• He **came **after she **had gone**.
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, the person took a certain direction and after some time he thought that he might have mistaken the direction.
 
• Thus, the first action will be in the past perfect tense i.e.** 'had mistaken'** and the second action will be in the simple past tense **'wondered'**.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2.**

**Correct Sentence:** ***He** **wondered** for a moment if he had mistaken the direction.*

questions.question:
**Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options, select the one that gives their correct order.**

A. This is because the Dar Assalam mosque in Berlin can welcome only a fraction of Muslim worshippers during Ramzan because of social distancing rules.

B. This year, a church in Berlin has opened its doors to let Muslims do Friday prayers while observing social distancing.

C. As Muslims around the world prepare to celebrate Id-ul-Fitr on 25th May, the holiday that marks the end of Ramzan, a month of fasting, things are very different.

D. The Martha Lutheran church has stepped in to help, saying, "We too have the same concerns. It's beautiful to feel that way about each other."
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'CBAD'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• While rearranging the given sentences, **we should look for some grammatical or contextual connections between the sentences-**__

 __
 
• **​**__**C will be the first sentence** as it is an independent sentence that is introducing the subject i.e. 'Muslims celebrating Ramzan'.
 
• **B will be the second sentence** as it is talking about a church opening its doors to let Muslims do Friday prayers.
 
• **A will be the third sentence **as it forms a mandatory pair with sentence B. The determiner** 'this'** in sentence A is referring to the situation explained in sentence B. 
 
• **D will be the last sentence** as it is elaborating more about a church welcoming Muslims to do Friday prayers. 
 
• Therefore,** option 2 **is the correct answer. 
 
 

**The correct order is:**

 
• **C: **As Muslims around the world prepare to celebrate Id-ul-Fitr on 25th May, the holiday that marks the end of Ramzan, a month of fasting, things are very different.
 
• **B: **This year, a church in Berlin has opened its doors to let Muslims do Friday prayers while observing social distancing.
 
• **A: **This is because the Dar Assalam mosque in Berlin can welcome only a fraction of Muslim worshippers during Ramzan because of social distancing rules.
 
• **D: **The Martha Lutheran church has stepped in to help, saying, "We too have the same concerns. It's beautiful to feel that way about each other."

• **Question tags** turn a statement into a question. They are often used for checking information that we think we know is true.
 
• Usually, if the main clause is positive, the question tag is negative, and if the main clause is negative, the question tag is positive. **Both** the main clause and the question tag must be in the **same tense**. 
 
• **Examples:**
 
 
• It's cold (positive), isn't it (negative)?
 
• It isn't cold (negative), is it (positive)? 
 
 
 
• According to the given explanation, we can understand that **'haven't you'** is the correct usage. 
 
• Therefore, **option 3** is the correct answer.
